hints.title: Longest Increasing Column Subsequence
hints.text: Minimizing column deletions is mathematically equivalent to maximizing the number of kept columns that are sorted in every row.

hints.title: Cross-Row Monotonicity Condition
hints.text: Column j can precede column i if and only if for every row string s, s[j] <= s[i].

hints.title: Dynamic Programming LIS on Columns
hints.text: Let dp[i] be the length of the longest valid column chain ending at column i. Initialize dp[i] = 1. For each j < i: if all(row[j] <= row[i] for row in strs), dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + 1). Return total columns minus max(dp).

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: C: number of columns in each string
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all 2^C column subsets is exponential and impossible for C = 100.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 1D dynamic programming on column indices computes the longest valid chain in O(C^2 * R) time using O(C) auxiliary array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the problem as a multi-string generalized Longest Increasing Subsequence.
complexity.notes: Every string must simultaneously satisfy the non-decreasing condition between chosen column pairs.
